Come, Follow Me · Job

“Yet Will I Trust in Him”

Job 1–3; 12–14; 19; 21–24; 38–40; 42

1

Theme One

“I know that my Redeemer liveth”

Where we are

By chapter 19, Job has lost his children, his wealth, and his health. His friends have spent chapters telling him it must be his fault.

This is the ash heap. Nothing has been fixed yet.

“

Scripture

“For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth: and though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God.”

Job 19:25–26

Léon Bonnat · Job · 1880

He says it from the ash heap, not after the happy ending.

A word worth knowing

The goel

In the law of Moses, the goel was the nearest kinsman who bought back what a family had lost: land, freedom, a future (Leviticus 25:25). It is the word behind Boaz in Ruth 4.

“Redeemer” is a family word. Job is saying: family is coming for me, even if every other court fails.

“

Hymn 136

“I know that my Redeemer lives. What comfort this sweet sentence gives!”

Its first line is Job 19:25. Handel opened the resurrection section of Messiah with the same words, and they have been sung at Easter ever since.

Samuel Medley · 1775

Discuss

What do you know that doesn’t depend on getting an explanation?

Discuss

What would you still believe on your worst day?

2

Theme Two

Seven days of silence

“

Scripture

“So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.”

Job 2:13

William Blake · Job’s Comforters · 1825

The silence was their best work. Then they started explaining.

“

Scripture

“I have heard many such things: miserable comforters are ye all.”

Thirty-five chapters of confident theology. The only thing worse than grief is grief with a lecture.

Job 16:2

“

What we signed up for

“Willing to bear one another’s burdens, that they may be light; yea, and are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort.”

Notice it doesn’t say “explain those that mourn.”

Mosiah 18:8–9

God’s verdict on the friends

Job 42:7

“Ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.”

The friends said correct-sounding things. Job said raw, honest things. God sides with Job. Comfort first; explanations later, or never.

Discuss

Why is presence so much harder than explanation?

Discuss

Your friend’s week just fell apart. What do you do in the first ten minutes?

Try it

Pair up. One person names something hard. The other may only sit with them. No fixing, no advice.

Sixty seconds. It is harder than it sounds, and it is the whole lesson.

3

Theme Three

The answer from the whirlwind

“

Scripture

“Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? … When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?”

Job 38:4, 7

William Blake · When the Morning Stars Sang Together · 1825

God’s answer is a tour of creation. Job is the small one at the bottom.

Read the speech closely

God never explains. He never mentions chapters 1 and 2. Job never learns why.

What Job gets instead is God.

“

Scripture

“I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee.”

Job 42:5

“

Liberty Jail · March 1839

“Know thou, my son, that all these things shall give thee experience, and shall be for thy good. The Son of Man hath descended below them all. Art thou greater than he?”

Joseph asked Job’s question: “O God, where art thou?” The answer came the same way: perspective, presence, promise. Not an explanation.

Doctrine and Covenants 122:7–8

DR

Elder Dale G. Renlund

“Infuriating Unfairness” · April 2021

“Do not let unfairness harden you or corrode your faith in God… Rather than becoming bitter, let Him help you become better.”

Discuss

Job never got an explanation. He got God. What changes when the answer is a Person?

Discuss

If God answered your biggest question with Himself, would that be enough?

“Though he slay me, yet will I trust in him.”

Job 13:15
